title: Product
meaning: The root of a set of specifications, its own space: its records link only to each other.

title: Stage
meaning: One of the five places a kind is read in, in order: domain model, use cases, interaction design, technical specification, test plan.

title: Designed, built, proved
meaning: An obligation's three states: its implementation specified, its technical record naming a file that exists, its test written at a level its kind allows.

title: Technical record
meaning: The one record of a technical kind that implements a design record, naming its file.

title: Product kind
meaning: A kind a product declares for itself, in any stage, under any kind.

title: Command layer
meaning: The commands every writer uses to change data (add, set, move, link, unlink, remove, apply), each one transaction that the store accepts or refuses whole.

title: Reference
meaning: Every kind, table, relation, stage and check of a product, generated from its schema and check rows.

title: Refusal
meaning: A write the store does not accept, with every reason and no data changed.

title: Recorded exception
meaning: Another aggregate of its domain that a command also changes in its transaction, named with the reason.

title: Pattern
meaning: Behavior several use cases share, written once with its rules and settings; each follower answers its settings.

title: Standard
meaning: Engineering rules the product's code follows, which technical records meet and standard rule tests prove.

title: Domain
meaning: A part of the product with its own model and language, for one business capability: its capabilities and use cases, glossary, domain services and repositories.

title: Aggregate
meaning: A cluster of entities changed together as one unit by one command at a time, with the invariants its own rule code enforces.

title: Domain event
meaning: Something that happened to an aggregate, in the past tense, with the fields it carries and the event type that delivers it.

title: Command
meaning: One intent on one aggregate: its handler loads the aggregate through its repository, holds it to its rules and saves it, or refuses with every reason.

title: Value object
meaning: A value with no identity, such as an email address, defined by its fields and checked by its constraints.

title: Specification
meaning: A named yes-or-no rule over aggregates of one domain, which commands check and queries select by.

title: Read model
meaning: A shape of data built for reading, from the aggregates it reads or the events it hears: its projection fills its table, and its queries read that table only through its reader.

title: Use case
meaning: One goal of an actor, with its requirements, its flows through the interfaces it happens in, and its tests.

title: View
meaning: A page or panel a flow's steps happen in, with its route and its view requirements.

title: Endpoint
meaning: The route that exposes one command or query, with its API requirements and handler.

title: Integration
meaning: An outside system the product exchanges with, through its adapter.

title: UI component
meaning: The code that draws the views it renders.

title: Business outcome
meaning: A measurable change the product exists to bring about, with its measure and target, which capabilities serve and tests measure.

title: Test data set
meaning: The starting records, environment and accounts some tests need, built with its aggregate's own commands.

title: Table
meaning: Where an entity's or read model's rows, or a domain's links, are stored, with its storage and keys.

title: Extension record
meaning: A record of a kind a product declares for itself, held to its kind's declaration.

title: Entry point
meaning: A file that starts the product or one of its processes, named as in code.

title: Tooling
meaning: A script or configuration that builds, checks or tests the product, named as in code.

title: Entity
meaning: A record the domain keeps, with an identity: its aggregate's root, which the aggregate is named for, or one of its children, reached only through the root. Its fields are typed by a basic type, a value object, or another aggregate by ID; its commands sit under it.

title: Invariant
meaning: A rule an aggregate always keeps, enforced by its own rule code before every save and proved by its test.

title: Repository
meaning: The one way an aggregate is loaded and saved whole, one per aggregate; a command handler reaches its aggregate only through it.

title: Capability
meaning: A lasting ability of the business that groups a domain's use cases, in order, and serves business outcomes.

title: Policy
meaning: A reaction under the command it runs, which hears one event: when that happens, run this command.

title: Query
meaning: A question asked of one read model, with the handler that answers it.

title: UC requirement
meaning: One rule a use case must keep, stated with MUST, SHOULD or MAY, fulfilled by its flows' steps and proved by its tests.

title: Flow
meaning: How a use case happens through one interface, as ordered steps on their paths, each invoking at most one command or query.

title: Interface
meaning: A way the product is used, such as the web app, the CLI or the MCP tools, that flows go through.

title: Role
meaning: Who acts in the product's use cases, such as the Owner, the Reader or an Agent.

title: Reader
meaning: The one way a query handler reaches its read model's storage, one per read model: an interface the handlers depend on, given to them by the query runner, reading only its read model's table, which its projection alone fills.

title: Check
meaning: One rule the engine applies on every load: a row of the `check` table whose query returns a row for each problem.

title: Problem
meaning: One thing a check found wrong or still to do in the loaded data. Problems are the result of a run, never stored.

title: Error
meaning: A problem that means the data is broken. `lathe check` exits 1 on any error.

title: Warning
meaning: A problem that means work is still to do. Warnings never fail `lathe check`.

title: Lathe's checks
meaning: The check rows that ship with Lathe, in `lathe/data/check.jsonl`, read-only to every product.

title: Product check
meaning: A check row a product adds for its own house rule, in its own `data/check.jsonl`.

title: Refused row
meaning: A row the store will not load or write, reported once as a `data-refused` error naming the file, the line and the rule.

title: Children limit
meaning: The most children of one kind a record of a product should hold: its `max_children` setting, 15 by default.

title: Lone child
meaning: The one record a capability or a group holds, which makes the level group nothing.

title: Entities limit
meaning: The most entities an aggregate of a product should hold: its `max_entities_per_aggregate` setting, 7 by default.

title: Page
meaning: One place in the app at its own address, showing one focus.

title: Address
meaning: A page's path and its `view` query parameter.

title: Focus
meaning: The product, domain, record or group a page is about.

title: Page stage
meaning: The one way a focus page draws its focus, full window behind the floating panels: Graph, ERD or Trace.

title: Space
meaning: One product as a place to work in, chosen from the rail.

title: Rail
meaning: The column of space icons at the far left of the nav.

title: Stage folder
meaning: One of a domain's five stages in the nav, listing its records by kind.

title: Kind group
meaning: The records of one kind in a stage or under a parent, shown together when there are several kinds to tell apart.

title: Map
meaning: A product's tree laid out once as boxes, which focusing never moves.

title: Depth
meaning: How many levels below the focus the camera frames.

title: Tab
meaning: One place in the desktop app's row of tabs, as a browser tab: its own focus, stage, view and Back and Forward. On the web the browser's own tabs are the tabs.

title: ERD
meaning: A domain's or an aggregate's model drawn as boxes and lines on the ERD stage.

title: Place
meaning: Where the Reader explores: the focus, stage, camera, depth, kind filters, the wiki card's open and expanded state and scroll, and its own Back and Forward history. One per browser tab on the web, one per tab in the desktop app.

title: Workbench
meaning: The wide-screen layout: panels a gap apart on the shell, every gap a resize handle.

title: Panel
meaning: A part of the app that floats over the stage, which a person shows, hides and resizes: the navigation, the tab panel or the wiki card.

title: Keymap
meaning: The one table of keyboard commands and their bindings, which every key, the palette, the sheet and every hint read.

title: Theme
meaning: A named set of token values with a light set and a dark set.

title: Color mode
meaning: System, Light or Dark: which of every theme's two sets shows.

title: Product folder
meaning: A folder with a `lathe.config.json` or a `data/` folder, which Lathe opens.

title: Product window
meaning: One desktop window showing one product folder.

title: App server
meaning: What a window or `lathe serve` serves Lathe from.

title: Write
meaning: One or more commands to the data, all taking effect or none.

title: Refusal reason
meaning: One reason the store refused a write or a load: the rule broken and where.

title: Record
meaning: One row of a kind's table, kept as one line of its data file: an ID unique across every kind, a title, at most one parent (none for the product and the kinds with no owner), typed columns, its part rows, and links as rows of each relation's table.

title: Kind
meaning: A sort of record, with its own table, stage, parents and ID pattern. Lathe has fifty; a product may declare more.

title: Parent
meaning: The one record a record sits under, named by one of its kind's parent columns.

title: Part
meaning: A row a record owns that is no record itself, such as an entity's fields or a table's keys, removed with it.

title: Link
meaning: A row of a relation's table joining two records of one product.

title: Relation
meaning: A sort of link, with the pairs of kinds it may join and its words read both ways.

title: Data file
meaning: `data/<table>.jsonl`: one table's rows, one JSON object per line, sorted by key. The source of truth, reviewed in git.

title: Obligation
meaning: A record that must be designed, built and proved: a constraint, invariant, specification, policy, domain service, UC requirement, view requirement, API requirement, pattern rule or standard rule, or a product's own obligation kind.

title: Designed
meaning: An obligation whose design is specified: a flow step fulfills the UC requirement, or a technical record implements the design record.

title: Built
meaning: A designed obligation whose implementing technical record names a file that exists.

title: Proved
meaning: An obligation with a test, automated or manual, at a level its kind allows.

title: Gap
meaning: An obligation that is not yet designed, built or proved, reported as a warning.

title: Run by
meaning: How a test runs: its level, its state, and its file or the reason it is manual.

title: Not automated yet
meaning: A test written before its code exists, to show what will prove an obligation. It never counts as proof.

title: Follower
meaning: A domain or use case that follows a pattern.

title: Owed
meaning: A pattern rule a domain must prove for itself, because it follows the rule's pattern.

title: Not applicable
meaning: A pattern rule a domain does not owe, because every following use case there marks its setting not applicable.

title: Waived
meaning: A pattern rule a domain does not owe, because no follower there gives a value that meets its applies-when setting.

title: Trace
meaning: The records that design, build and prove one obligation, and the files they name.
